newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian minister resigns after conflict row.
newsitem.headline: Australian minister resigns after conflict row.

text.p: A junior Australian minister announced his resignation on Friday after lingering conflict of interest accusations, prompting Prime Minister John Howard to carry out a minor cabinet reshuffle.

Small Business Minister Geoff Prosser offered his resignation after an opposition campaign to unseat him over his continued involvement in three shopping malls he owns in the state of Western Australia.
Government guidelines, which Prosser denied having breached, prevent ministers from daily business activities and from being involved in decisions which affect their business interests.

"Over the past few weeks, the media and the opposition have sought to make my presence in the Ministry the focus of attention rather than the the broader policy issues and achievements of your government," Prosser told Howard in a resignation letter.

"I appreciate that this is now distracting the community and diverting government resources and energy from the central task we have at hand -- that of job creation and revitalising the small business sector," he added.

Howard said in a statement that Prosser's main duties would be assumed by Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith, who would retain his current duties and become Minister for Workplace Relations and Small Business.

Howard also appointed Western Australian Senator Chris Ellison as the new Minister for Customs and Consumer Affairs, both areas previously the responsibility of Prosser. He announced several minor appointments including that of lower house parliamentarian Neil Andrew as chief government whip.
